chunks: And from him, from Safwan ibn Yahya and Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding a man who has intercourse with his wife after he has concluded the Ihram (state of consecration) but has not yet said the Talbiyah, he said: 'There is no penalty upon him.'

key_terms.إِحْرَام: State of consecration for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.شَيْء: Thing, penalty, or expiation in this legal context
key_terms.يُلَبِّ: To recite the Talbiyah (declaration of intent)

ai.seo_question: What is the penalty for a pilgrim who has sex before reciting the Talbiyah?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies that the obligation of expiation (damm) for sexual intercourse during Hajj is contingent upon the formal commencement of the ritual state via the Talbiyah. Consequently, intercourse prior to this declaration is treated as a permissible act within the sacred boundaries, reflecting the Shia juristic view that the specific prohibitions of Ihram activate only upon the utterance of the Talbiyah or the completion of the initial Tawaf, rather than merely the wearing of the garments.
